title: Teaching & Academic Service
text:
Selected training
My methodological training includes Bayesian phylogenetic inference with BEAST2, statistical methods for linguistics and psychology, Gaussian processes and uncertainty quantification, machine learning, text analytics, reproducible research, and scientific computing on Linux/HPC systems.

title: Research
text: My research focuses on how linguistic structures emerge, change, and persist through time. I combine historical and comparative linguistics with quantitative modelling, phylogenetic methods, and cross-linguistic typology.

title: Research
text:
Syntax and linguistic evolution
A central strand of my work concerns the evolution of syntactic hierarchy, especially in clause-linkage constructions. I am interested in how relations between clauses vary across languages, how those structures evolve, and how syntactic organization interacts with semantics.
My doctoral dissertation, Syntactic Hierarchy in Linguistic Evolution: A Phylogenetic View of Clause-Linkage, developed a phylogenetic perspective on these questions.

title: Research
text:
Comparative typology and phylogenetics
I use Bayesian phylogenetic inference and phylogenetic comparative methods to investigate historical dependencies in cross-linguistic data. This work addresses questions that are difficult to answer from synchronic typological distributions alone, because related languages are not statistically independent observations.
Methodologically, my work includes:

Bayesian phylogenetic inference
phylogenetic comparative methods
Bayesian hierarchical modelling
Gaussian processes
comparative typology
corpus-based quantitative analysis

title: Research
text:
Historical and Semitic linguistics
My broader research background includes Semitic languages, historical phonology, Hebrew and Aramaic varieties, and transcription systems. I have worked on Biblical Hebrew rhotics, Mandaic transcription and annotation, and comparative resources for Semitic transcription and transliteration.

title: Research
text:
Computational modelling
I also work with computational approaches to historical linguistics and language evolution. Earlier work included neural proto-language reconstruction, while more recent work combines computational modelling with typological and phylogenetic data.

title: Research
text:
Technical methods
I work primarily with R, Python, and SQL, with statistical modelling in Stan and phylogenetic analysis in BEAST2. My research workflow uses Git, Linux, Slurm/HPC, Quarto, R Markdown, Pandoc, and LaTeX.

title: Carlo Y. Meloni
text:
I am a postdoctoral researcher at the Chair of Multilingual Computational Linguistics at the University of Passau, where I work on the ProduSemy project.

My research investigates linguistic evolution, with a particular focus on syntax and on how hierarchical structures change over time. Methodologically, I combine comparative typology, Bayesian phylogenetic inference, and computational modelling to study cross-linguistic patterns and their historical development.
I completed my PhD at the Institute for the Interdisciplinary Study of Language Evolution (ISLE), University of Zurich. My dissertation, Syntactic Hierarchy in Linguistic Evolution: A Phylogenetic View of Clause-Linkage, examined the emergence and diachronic behaviour of clause-linkage structures.

title: Launch checklist
text:
Launch checklist
Before making the repository public and enabling GitHub Pages:

Run quarto preview and inspect every page.
Run quarto render and make sure the docs/ directory is created.
Check that docs/index.html exists.
Check that the CV download works locally.
Verify your preferred public email address.
Verify the University of Passau, CALC Lab, ORCID, Google Scholar, and GitHub links.
Review the publication list against your latest CV and Scholar/ORCID records.
Decide whether to keep the CALC-hosted profile photo or store a local copy in images/.
Remove anything from the repository that you do not want to become public.
Commit and push the latest source files and rendered docs/ files.
Change repository visibility from Private to Public if using GitHub Free.
In GitHub: Settings > Pages > Build and deployment.
Set Source to Deploy from a branch.
Set Branch to main and Folder to /docs.
Save and wait for the deployment to complete.
Visit https://cymelo92.github.io in a private/incognito browser window.
